candidates.name: Baserate: redemption-free BTC→MUSD credit and composable sMUSD on Mezo's own Morpho
candidates.one_liner: A correct ERC-4626 over sMUSD (wsMUSD), the first BTC→MUSD market on Mezo's Morpho Blue, and a Vault V2 MUSD lending vault whose idle cash always earns the sMUSD rate. Around them: one-transaction borrowing from a faucet drip, a B.AMM-style liquidation backstop, a one-signature claim-and-borrow for stranded CollSurplusPool BTC, and a drop-in sMUSD strategy Mezo can switch on with one call.
candidates.problem:
Retail MUSD credit is gone, and the composable rails that could replace it are empty.
- Troves fell from 104 (6.03M MUSD debt, 2025-11-30) to 1 (14.5k); getTroveOwnersCount() = 1 on a re-read today. MUSD has traded at $0.9885–0.9911 for 60 days, below the ≈$0.9925 redemption floor, and 681 redemptions burned 1.28M MUSD in ≈30 days, so any new trove with a lower ratio than the survivor is first in the queue. A minimum trove needs ≈0.027 BTC, 27× the 0.001 BTC faucet drip.
- Mezo's Morpho Blue has one market (BTC/mUSDC: 81.9k supplied, 66.3k borrowed, ≈81% utilised) and holds 0 MUSD (re-read today). USDC credit is capped by the 122k mUSDC supply. Morpho MUSD markets on every chain hold under $100.
- sMUSD (7,382,555 supply) is not ERC-4626, so it cannot be collateral. The only submitted wrapper (Mezo Flow) targets a deposit(assets, receiver) that does not exist.
- sMUSD's yield is about to fall. 57–63% of its last-30-day inflow (two independent ideator reads) was redemption-fee BTC routed through YieldConverter, and that stream ends with ≈12.5k MUSD of redemption capacity left. Enclave interest alone (14.52M × 1% × 50%) is ≈1.0% on 7.38M [I]. The VaultGauge's 58,981 MUSD backlog (re-read today), which funds 10,000 MUSD/week to veBTC voters, lasts ≈6–9 weeks [I]. All 7.38M of principal sits in IdleStrategy at 0% (strategy() re-read today), although MUSDSavingsRate was built with a pluggable IVaultStrategy.
- 5.70 BTC (≈$459k) of redemption surplus is unclaimed in CollSurplusPool across 27 accounts.
- Liquidation depth binds any BTC-collateral market. The MUSD side of BTC/MUSD is ≈$55k (vAMM 39.3k + CL200 15.7k). 0.2 BTC sells for 15,982 MUSD on CL200, while the vAMM pays 27.8% under oracle for the same size.
candidates.mechanism:
Core (Wave 2):
1. wsMUSD: an immutable OpenZeppelin ERC-4626 over sMUSD 0xb4D4…51CC, with decimalsOffset and dead shares against inflation attacks, and no ERC-2771.
- deposit pulls MUSD (EIP-2612 permit) and calls sMUSD.deposit(amount). It never stakes in VaultGauge 0x6778…a401, because staking sends the MUSD yield to voters and pays ≈0.77% in MEZO instead.
- harvest() is permissionless and runs at least daily: PCV.distributeMUSD() (permissionless), sMUSD.claimYield(), then re-deposit. Harvested yield vests linearly over 7 days (xERC4626), so the share price is smooth for oracles and jumps from donations or distributions cannot be sandwiched.
- Pending yield is exact and public: claimableYield(this) + balance × (yieldIndex − supplyYieldIndex(this)) / 1e18 (claimableYield is a stored mapping).
- redeem calls sMUSD.withdraw(), which auto-claims; exit is instant and 1:1.
2. Oracles (immutable Morpho IOracle, 1e36 scale).
- BtcMusdOracle reads the Skip BTC/USD precompile 0x7b7c…0015 (latestRoundData; updatedAt is the current block) and reverts if the price is older than 60 s. That matches PriceFeed, which also has no fallback.
- Pyth BTC on 0x5D28… is used only as a ±10% sanity band, and only when it is no older than 3,900 s. Mezo's pusher updates Pyth on a heartbeat: BTC and MUSD were last pushed together ≈12 minutes before today's read. So the inputs' 2–3% deviation guard would false-trip in fast markets, and a Pyth fallback would liquidate on a price up to an hour old.
- The MUSD leg is max(1, min(Pyth MUSD 0x0617…c6de no older than 3,900 s, 1.02)), or 1.00 if stale. BTC is therefore never valued above par-MUSD terms while MUSD < $1.
- WsMusdOracle (for M2) = wsMUSD.convertToAssets(1e18) × min(Pyth MUSD, 1), with share-price growth capped at 10%/yr.
- Both read the live Pyth Core Compatible contracts (0x5D28… mainnet, 0x933a… testnet), never the stale docs address 0x2880….
3. Markets, created with permissionless Morpho.createMarket on 0x5658…A311 using AdaptiveCurveIrm 0x3760…c1e7 at LLTV 0.86e18, the only enabled pair (re-read today). Testnet: Morpho 0xCe1d…5a73, IRM 0x0c97…7441, LLTV 0.77e18.
- M1: BTC precompile 0x7b7C…0000 as collateral, MUSD as the loan. No redemption queue, no minimum debt, no capacity lock.
- M2 (module): wsMUSD as collateral, mUSDC as the loan. It is the first market to take sMUSD as collateral, letting savers raise USDC without selling MUSD into the ≈$20k Mezo-native bid.
4. vMUSD lending vault: a Morpho Vault V2 from VaultV2Factory.createVaultV2 (mainnet 0xA64f…, testnet 0x25eB…; both deployed, re-read today). It uses the same template as Mezo's USDC Lending Vault (Vault V2 0x0629… → MorphoMarketV1AdapterV2 0xb0EE…).
- A MorphoMarketV1AdapterV2 supplies M1. An ERC-4626 adapter into wsMUSD (Morpho's vault adapter pattern, deployed from GPL source if no factory exists on Mezo [U]) is the liquidityAdapter, so idle MUSD always earns the sMUSD rate and exits instantly.
- A permissionless allocator moves MUSD into M1 only while M1's supply APY beats wsMUSD's trailing APY. That makes the sMUSD rate the base rate of BTC credit on Mezo, the DSR→Spark pattern [I].
- Caps are liquidity-aware: M1's absolute cap tracks backstop MUSD plus the BTC size that QuoterV2 0x4e56… says clears on CL200 within the liquidation incentive. Cap increases wait 48 h; the sentinel can only cut caps or deallocate. A 10% performance fee goes to a FeeRouter.
5. One-transaction borrowing (BorrowAccount): per-user EIP-1167 clones from a CREATE2 factory (salt = owner).
- Mezo's gas token is also the ERC-20 at 0x7b7C…0000, with one shared balance. So openAndBorrow{value: BTC}(amount, maxLtvBps) has the clone approve Morpho, supplyCollateral(onBehalf = clone) and borrow(onBehalf = clone, receiver = owner), then require LTV ≤ min(maxLtv, LLTV − 15 pts).
- repayAndWithdraw uses MUSD permit.
- Clones are owner-only and immutable, and need no Morpho authorization over the user.
6. Liquidations.
- Backstop (bMUSD, an ERC-4626 over MUSD kept idle in wsMUSD): a port of thUSD's MIT B.Protocol BAMM.sol and PriceFormula, retargeted from the Stability Pool to Morpho.
- Anyone calls liquidate(borrower). The backstop redeems wsMUSD just in time and calls Morpho.liquidate on M1 (incentive ≈4.38% at 0.86, ≈7.4% at 0.77).
- It resells seized BTC through an oracle-anchored swap with a decaying discount, plus keeper sales on CL200 0x9CBc… via CLSwapRouter 0x37cD…, only within a price-impact bound. It never dumps into the vAMM.
- A permissionless flash liquidator (onMorphoLiquidate callback) runs when DEX depth alone clears the position.
7. Come-back flow for the 27 redeemed-out accounts.
- The UI reads CollSurplusPool.getCollateral(user).
- An EOA signs an EIP-712 ClaimCollateral for BorrowerOperationsSignatures 0xB57a…df7a, with recipient = its BorrowAccount. The factory calls claimCollateralWithSignature(borrower, account, sig, deadline).
- The BTC lands in the clone via receive(); the clone supplies it to M1 and optionally borrows.
- Smart-account owners call claimCollateral() and deposit.

Modules (Wave 2 stretch):
8. EscapeHatch (trove → Morpho), with honest scope. Mainnet has one trove and the last trove cannot close, so its mainnet market today is zero. It is a primitive for future troves and a full testnet demo (307 troves).
- The user signs CloseTrove (recipient = EscapeHatch) plus a Morpho setAuthorizationWithSig, or migrates into their BorrowAccount.
- The flash source is Morpho.flashLoan (fee-free) once M1 holds the debt. Until then it is CLPool.flash on mUSDC/MUSD CL10 0xCC37…, which holds 5.33M MUSD at a 0.05% fee (re-read today).
- Sequence: flash debt − 200 → closeTroveWithSignature (burns our MUSD; the BTC arrives via receive()) → supplyCollateral(onBehalf) → borrow(onBehalf) → repay the flash. The contract enforces the user's min-collateral and max-LTV bounds, because trove signatures carry no price conditions.
- An optional keeper-triggered mode executes a pre-signed escape only when Pyth MUSD < 0.9925 and the trove sits within a configurable redemption depth (SortedTroves.getLast/getPrev, HintHelpers.getRedemptionHints).
- It reverts cleanly in Recovery Mode and on the last trove. A trove whose LTV exceeds the LLTV (ICR below ≈116% at 0.86, below ≈130% at 0.77) needs a top-up first.
9. sMUSD strategy packet: BufferedLendingStrategy implements sMUSD's IVaultStrategy {allocate, deallocate, claimYield, migrate, onMigrated}.
- It keeps ≥75% of principal idle, so deallocate is always exact and instant even if the VaultGauge's 72% exits at once. It supplies at most 25% (and never more than vMUSD's M1 cap) to vMUSD.
- claimYield returns 0 unless realized, liquid interest exceeds a dust floor. This matters because sMUSD calls strategy.claimYield() without try/catch inside every deposit and withdraw, and _receiveYield reverts AmountTooSmall when amount × 1e18 / totalSupply rounds to 0 (verified in source today). A naive strategy would brick sMUSD.
- Activation is one owner call, sMUSD.setStrategy(strategy), by 0x98D8…7C7a, delivered as a mainnet-fork-tested packet.
10. Fee loop: the FeeRouter splits fees three ways.
- Part is donated to every sMUSD holder through the permissionless sMUSD.receiveProtocolYield; 72% of that accrues to the VaultGauge and reaches veBTC voters through FeesVotingReward 0x33b8….
- Part is posted as MUSD incentives on the BTC/MUSD pool gauges, deepening the liquidation venue (S1).
- The rest is treasury.

Phase 3 (after the hackathon; S2):
11. Lending-gauge sidecar.
- veBTC holders vote on vMUSD's per-market allocations among curator-approved markets (M1, M2, and Lockstep's pool if built). Votes are keyed by tokenId, with voting power read at epoch start and no custody.
- The sidecar holds Vault V2's allocator role, so votes move liquidity only inside curator caps.
- Voters earn a share of the performance fee from the markets they back, vesting over 4 epochs. Bad debt in a market forfeits its backers' unvested rewards to lenders.
- It migrates onto a PoolsVoter vault gauge if governance creates one.

candidates.composable_outputs:
- wsMUSD: the first correct ERC-4626 over sMUSD, usable as Morpho collateral, as an LP asset, or as a Pendle-style PT/YT base.
- vMUSD: an ERC-4626 Vault V2 share paying the higher of credit interest and the sMUSD rate. It is structurally eligible for a vault gauge, exactly like Mezo's USDC Lending Vault.
- bMUSD: backstop shares that earn liquidation premiums on top of the savings rate.
- M1 and M2 market IDs that any Morpho curator, vault, bot or front end can use. Idle MUSD in M1 becomes Mezo's first fee-free MUSD flash liquidity (MUSD has no ERC-3156).
- BtcMusdOracle and WsMusdOracle: reusable IOracle and Chainlink-shaped feeds with staleness and sanity guards.
- The BorrowAccount factory, the come-back claim-and-borrow primitive, and EscapeHatch, all callable by any front end or keeper.
- BufferedLendingStrategy: a drop-in IVaultStrategy Mezo can activate with one call.
- A Goldsky subgraph and a TypeScript SDK, needed because Morpho's API does not index chain 31612.
candidates.business_model:
Who pays:
- BTC borrowers pay AdaptiveCurveIrm interest: 4% at the 90% utilisation target at launch, then adaptive (the same IRM prices Mezo's USDC market at ≈3.3–3.5%). In return they get no redemption exposure, no minimum debt, and a 4.38% liquidation incentive instead of losing up to ≈10% over debt in a trove liquidation.
- M2 borrowers pay mUSDC interest.
- Liquidated borrowers pay the incentive to the backstop.
- Migrations pay 0.1% of migrated debt.

Who earns:
- vMUSD lenders earn max(credit interest, sMUSD rate), less a 10% performance fee. bMUSD depositors add liquidation premiums.
- Every sMUSD holder benefits through fee donations now, and through the strategy if Mezo activates it. Rule of thumb [I]: each $1M lent at ≈3.5% is ≈$35k/yr of new MUSD income, ≈+0.47 pp on 7.38M sMUSD, of which the VaultGauge's 72% reaches veBTC voters. That replaces the redemption-fee stream that is ending.

MUSD demand:
- Lenders must source MUSD, typically by buying at ≈0.989 on Tigris.
- Every M1 loan is structural future MUSD demand: the role the 104 troves used to play, without redemption risk.

Honest scale: retail BTC credit on Mezo today is the $66k borrowed in the BTC/mUSDC market, so year-one fees are thousands of dollars. The value is restoring retail MUSD credit and giving sMUSD a real yield source before the cliff.

Go-to-market:
1. The 27 accounts holding 5.70 BTC of surplus (146 accounts have ever had some), via the come-back flow: 'reclaim your BTC and borrow without redemption risk'.
2. BTC/mUSDC borrowers capped by the 122k mUSDC supply.
3. sMUSD's 448 holders, and Enclave A, whose ≈5.26M single-sided MUSD range sits out of range and earns nothing: 'same floor, plus credit interest'.
4. Ask Mezo for a vMUSD vault gauge (the USDC Lending Vault precedent) and hand over the strategy packet.
5. Ignition, then Founder grants; a third-party audit for a Mezo Market listing.
candidates.differentiation:
- Mezodot (submitted, high threat, testnet): a bespoke omnichain money market with ≈111 KB of new, unaudited Solidity. Baserate writes no lending engine. Its new code (wrapper, oracles, clones, allocator, backstop, migrator) sits on Mezo's own Morpho Blue and Vault V2, and it ships to mainnet with caps.
- Cosign (pipeline): Morpho first-loss cover with MEZO collateral, a stated judge red flag at ≈$2.95M FDV. Baserate takes only BTC and wsMUSD as collateral. Its Phase-3 sidecar is a route to Luongo's lending gauge with no MEZO collateral.
- Mezo Flow, MUSD Yield Vault, Morbit: Mezo Flow is coded against a 4626 interface sMUSD lacks and is tested only on a mock. The other two wrap a Stability Pool that has seen 28 liquidations ever. wsMUSD is fork-tested against the real yieldIndex and claim semantics, and is the only wrapper used both as collateral and as a vault's liquidity floor.
- Pylon, Coil, MezoRoute, Lifeline, Vigil: all keep users in troves, which are first in the mainnet redemption queue while MUSD < 0.9925. Baserate removes the queue and offers a one-signature exit from it.
- Mezo's USDC Lending Vault lends mUSDC and is capped by the 122k supply. Baserate is its MUSD counterpart on the same template, opening the 29.5M-MUSD side.
- Mezo's own Morpho oracle checks only that the answer is above 0 [ideator V]. Baserate's oracles revert on staleness, which is the guard judges look for.
- The abandoned 'Mezo Morpho MSTR/COIN…' MUSD vaults (EOA-curated, redeemed to 1 wei on 2026-06-26) used exotic collateral, with no savings floor and no backstop.
- Ditto dMUSD exports MUSD to Spark on Ethereum; Baserate keeps it working on Mezo.
- Mezo's roadmap promises 'a broader suite of lending markets'. Because Baserate uses Mezo's exact stack, adopting it is a configuration change for Mezo, not a competitor.
candidates.testnet_feasibility:
Borrower features: yes, with faucet funds only. 0.001 BTC at the testnet LLTV of 0.77 supports ≈$62, so a judge borrows ≈40 MUSD at 50% LTV in one transaction carrying the BTC as msg.value. Testnet Morpho has 0.77 and IRM 0x0c97… enabled and holds 0 MUSD today (re-read), so we seed the market.

Judge path (≈5 minutes):
1. Faucet.
2. openAndBorrow 40 MUSD.
3. Risk desk: Skip and Pyth ages, liquidation price, incentive, the depth-derived cap, 'redemption risk: none'.
4. Deposit dispenser MUSD into vMUSD and watch the split between M1 and wsMUSD.
5. Post wsMUSD into M2 and borrow mUSDC.
6. Repay and withdraw everything in one transaction.
7. Evidence tab.

We must provide:
1. ≈20–50k test MUSD for M1 and vMUSD liquidity, the backstop, and a dispenser (100–200 MUSD per address per day). Source: a Mezo DevRel grant of test BTC or MUSD. Fallback: pooled faucet drips swapped on the testnet MUSD/BTC pool 0xd16A… (102.6M MUSD / 1,303 BTC), plus gas compensation from liquidating the two testnet troves below 110% ICR.
2. Test mUSDC for M2. The 10.08M supply sits with Mezo's deployer and has no public mint, so we request some or buy from the testnet stable pool 0x525F… at ≈0.844.
3. A yield simulator. Testnet sMUSD has pcv = 0 and vaultGauge = 0 (re-read today), so the keeper makes labelled receiveProtocolYield donations sized to mainnet's rate.
4. Canary positions near LLTV, so judges can call the backstop's liquidate when real Skip moves cross them. Edge cases (Skip outage, Recovery Mode, last trove, backstop solvency) run as Foundry fork tests.
5. Sponsored trove kits for EscapeHatch. Our contract calls openTroveWithSignature, supplying ≈0.03–0.04 test BTC, so the judge owns a trove at ≥140% ICR, then pre-signs CloseTrove and migrates in one click. The trove must sit below 0.77 LTV with margin; the 120%-ICR kit proposed in one input cannot migrate at 0.77.
6. The come-back flow is shown on a mainnet fork, since judges hold no surplus. An optional testnet kit has our bot fully redeem a sponsored trove to create a real CollSurplusPool balance.
7. The strategy runs on our own MUSDSavingsRate (MIT) instance on testnet, because setStrategy on the real testnet sMUSD is owner-gated, plus a mainnet-fork transcript.
candidates.mainnet_plan:
Wave 1 slice (by 2026-10-26 15:00 UTC): BtcMusdOracle, testnet M1, BorrowAccount one-transaction borrow and repay, wsMUSD on testnet, a minimal UI, and fork tests against mainnet state.

Wave 2 (Nov 2–15): mainnet deployment on 0x5658….
- M1 at 0.86; M2 if mUSDC supply is secured.
- wsMUSD capped at 50k MUSD. Its only admin power is raising that cap, behind a 72 h timelock.
- vMUSD capped at 100k. M1's absolute cap starts at ≈25k and is scripted to backstop MUSD plus 0.2-BTC clean-liquidation depth.
- Per-account collateral ≤0.2 BTC and opening LTV ≤71%. Backstop ≤50k. EscapeHatch ≤20k MUSD per transaction.
- Seed ≈10k MUSD (bought on Tigris) and 0.1 BTC of team funds, so real loans exist.
- Keeper live: harvest, allocator, liquidations. Pyth pushes only if a Hermes API key is obtained [U], because public Hermes now returns 401.
- BufferedLendingStrategy deployed inactive, with the setStrategy packet and simulated outcomes sent to Mezo.

Security:
- Immutable oracles, wrapper, clones and EscapeHatch; Vault V2 timelocks.
- A 2-of-3 Safe sentinel that can pause deposits and new borrows or cut caps, but never blocks exits.
- Foundry fork, fuzz and invariant suites: wsMUSD assets ≥ claims with a monotone share price; clones hold no MUSD after any call; caps never exceeded; backstop share value conserved; strategy deallocation exact.
- Slither and Aderyn, an AI audit with a public findings ledger, and a threat model.
- Verified on Blockscout and Sourcify, plus an evidence page of every transaction.

After the hackathon:
- Raise caps with backstop size and Tigris depth.
- Third-party audit, then a Mezo Market listing.
- The vault-gauge and strategy proposals.
- The Phase-3 lending gauge.
- Ignition and Founder grants.
candidates.key_risks:
1. Demand. Borrowing MUSD to sell at ≈0.989 into thin USDC liquidity is unattractive, and Mezo's own MUSD Morpho vaults were wound down. Lenders lose nothing versus sMUSD, but utilisation may start low.
2. The floor itself is falling. Once redemption fees stop, sMUSD earns ≈1% [I], so 'never below sMUSD' is a weak promise unless borrower interest, or the strategy, replaces that stream.
3. Liquidation depth. ≈$55k of MUSD-side BTC/MUSD depth forces small caps and may leave the backstop holding BTC inventory. Morpho markets cannot be paused, and bad debt is socialised to lenders.
4. Oracles. A Skip outage freezes borrows and liquidations (the CDP has the same exposure). Pyth MUSD updates only on a 1% move or hourly, and public Hermes now refuses update data without a key, so we cannot push fresher prices ourselves.
5. sMUSD is an upgradeable multisig proxy. A native 4626 upgrade would make wsMUSD redundant, and an interface change could break it.
6. The strategy is governance-gated, and the multisig may never call setStrategy. A mis-sized buffer could make sMUSD withdrawals revert; the 75% buffer and the invariant tests guard against this.
7. EscapeHatch has no mainnet market today: there is one trove, and it cannot close. Trove signatures are ECDSA-only, with one nonce and no cancel.
8. Competition. Mezo may ship its own MUSD market, Cosign may submit a Morpho MUSD market, and Mezodot already claims 'lending market for MUSD'.
9. Scope. This is the largest build in the slate: the core (items 1–7) is L, the full scope XL.
10. Concentration. Enclave A's veBTC #6114 unlocks 2026-11-12, mid-Wave 2, and its 5.25M sMUSD and 5.26M of CL MUSD could move.

candidates.name: BoostBook: a priced, delivery-verified boost market between veMEZO and veBTC
candidates.one_liner: veMEZO holders rent boost to veBTC holders for MUSD at a uniform weekly clearing price. Each fill settles atomically in Mezo's own BoostVoter (vote, MUSD bribe, pokeBoost, PoolsVoter.poke) from per-owner accounts that never pool or transfer NFTs. It gives MEZO's main utility its first market price and its first MUSD cash flow.
candidates.problem:
Boost is MEZO's main productive use, and it is barely priced or paid.
- MEZO is ≈$0.0029 (−98% from its ATH; market cap ≈$1.47M). veMEZO locks 280.69M MEZO across 1,376 holders and earns rebases in MEZO, but almost no dollars.
- Boost bribes totalled ≈$464 over three weeks (2 deposits). MEZO Gauges have never been bribed. VeMezoPool buys veMEZO at 50% of face.
- Boost is under-used:
  - non-permanent veBTC averages ≈1.06x;
  - 719 boost gauges exist for 6,161 veBTC NFTs;
  - ≈38.9M of 98.72M veMEZO voting power is on no boost gauge (BoostVoter totalWeight 59.82M, re-read today).
- Boost is cheap relative to its value. A 5x boost on a 1-BTC max lock needs ≈155k veMEZO VP (≈$450). A sMUSD-gauge voter earns ≈44 MUSD per boosted unit per week today (10,000 MUSD over 225.8 units), so 5x on 1 BTC is worth ≈177 MUSD/week now.
- Demand is stated: Mezo Academy says institutional veBTC 'must source veMEZO', Enclave #6114 (500 BTC) sits at 1x with no boost gauge, and Mezo wrote that no automated veMEZO strategies exist.
- Matchbox and native addBribes are pay-and-pray: no price, no guaranteed delivery, no refund.

Honest headwind: the per-unit value is funded by the sMUSD gauge's 58,981 MUSD backlog, which lasts ≈6–9 weeks. After that, per-unit income falls to ≈15 MUSD/week if redemption fees continue, or ≈4–5 if they stop [I].
candidates.mechanism:
1. The commodity.
- BoostVoter computes boost = min(5, 1 + 4·(U/u)·(w/M)) (verified in the BoostVoter source today). U = VeBTC.unboostedTotalVotingPower(), u = the NFT's unboosted VP, w = weights[its boost gauge], M = VeMEZO.totalVotingPower().
- The extra veBTC VP that w buys is u·(boost − 1) = 4·U·w/M. Below the 5x cap this does not depend on which NFT receives it.
- Boost is therefore fungible, and a uniform-price auction is the right market. Live values U = 636.55 and M = 98.72M mean 1M veMEZO VP adds ≈25.8 boosted units.
2. Sellers.
- A veMEZO (VeMEZO 0xb90f…E122) moves into its owner's BoostAccount, an EIP-1167 clone of one immutable implementation. Only the owner can withdraw, and only outside epochs it has sold.
- The account sets a reserve price in MUSD per 1k VP per epoch. It compounds rebases (RewardsDistributor 0x0751… claim) and casts the owner's separate ThirdPartyVoter (MEZO Gauges) vote; veMEZO votes both voters at full weight.
- No pooled token and no pooled custody: one NFT per account.
3. Buyers.
- The veBTC (VeBTC 0x3D4b…F279) stays in the buyer's wallet.
- The owner calls BoostVoter.createBoostGauge(GaugeFactory 0x4150…CCAd, tokenId, [], []) once. The source accepts empty arrays; the caller must be owner or approved, and the NFT must be NORMAL or MANAGED and either unexpired or permanent.
- The owner then calls bid(tokenId, units, maxPrice, epochs), escrowing MUSD by permit. Units are capped at the remaining 5x headroom.
4. Clearing.
- Settlement runs once per epoch, late in the vote window, before epochVoteEnd (after that, only whitelisted NFTs may vote).
- A permissionless settle() accepts a keeper-submitted solution sorted by price and verifies it in O(n): prices are monotone, filled units ≤ supply S = (4U/M) × offered VP, and every excluded bid is below the clearing price p*.
- Every winner pays p*.
- Settlement is chunked under the 10M block gas limit and the 30-gauge vote limit.
5. Atomic delivery and payment in Mezo's contracts. Each chunk:
- each matched BoostAccount calls BoostVoter.vote(veMEZOId, buyerGauges, weights), once per epoch as onlyNewEpoch enforces;
- the book calls BoostVoter.addBribes(buyerGauge, [MUSD], [rent]); MUSD is whitelisted on mainnet and testnet (re-read today);
- BoostVoter.pokeBoosts(buyers) and PoolsVoter.poke(buyerId) apply the boost to the buyer's pool votes, so it counts in that epoch's fee rewards;
- VeBTC.votingPowerOfNFT is read before and after, and undelivered units are refunded from escrow.
Sellers' accounts call BoostVoter.claimBribes after the epoch.
6. Dilution guard. Outside veMEZO voters on a buyer's gauge would share the bribe. Late settlement leaves them about an hour to do so. The book reports the realized price per seller, and a direct-escrow payout mode (from Torque) pays sellers per delivered unit if dilution becomes material.
7. Expiry enforcement.
- Votes persist across epochs, and boosts stay cached until poked.
- At each epoch flip a keeper re-votes or resets seller accounts, then calls BoostVoter.pokeBoost and PoolsVoter.poke on former lessees, so stale boosts cannot free-ride (Thesis Defense #3/#4/#5).
- Batches stay bounded (Halborn 7.8), and a share of the take rate pays the keeper bounty.
8. Instant fills. A few reserve accounts stay unvoted each epoch, so a new buyer can be filled at the last p* within minutes. This is also the judge path.
9. Buyer automation (optional EarnAccount): an immutable per-owner account that holds the veBTC and votes it, so delegation needs no ERC-721 approval. It:
- chooses PoolsVoter and ValidatorsVoter votes from last epoch's realized reward per unit (tokenRewardsPerEpoch on each FeesVotingReward and BribeVotingReward), with hysteresis;
- calls increaseUnlockTime weekly, or lockPermanent;
- sweeps claimFeesAndBribes and RewardsDistributor claims to the owner or into sMUSD;
- holds a boost budget of at most x% of last epoch's MUSD rewards (pay-from-yield).
Reward contracts pay ownerOf, so the account receives the rewards and forwards them.
10. BoostPriceOracle stores p* per epoch and a 4-epoch TWAP.
11. A 5% take rate funds poke bounties. The rest buys MEZO on MEZO/MUSD CL200 0x1D6e…, capped by its ≈1.4k MUSD of depth, and locks it permanently (createLock + lockPermanent) as protocol-owned veMEZO, which also sells boost.

candidates.composable_outputs:
- BoostPriceOracle: an on-chain price per epoch, plus a TWAP, for one veMEZO-VP-week of boost. It is the first market price for MEZO's utility: lenders can value veMEZO by its cash flow rather than MEZO spot, and veBTC credit (C3) can price boost-funded repayment.
- BoostAccount and EarnAccount standards: vote-only delegation without transfer rights, with an IEarnStrategy hook that Matchbox, Boar, Lockwatch-style tools or Mezo's app can plug into.
- A permissionless 'buy boost' entry point that any contract owning veBTC (Boar's relay, a vault, an Enclave Safe) can call on a schedule.
- Settlement events, and a subgraph of realized reward per vote-unit by gauge and epoch.
- Protocol-owned permanent veMEZO that itself supplies boost.
candidates.business_model:
Who pays: veBTC holders rent boost in MUSD, retail and managed relays alike (Boar #1226 is already 5x; Aurove #6107).

Who earns: veMEZO sellers get MUSD through native bribes on top of rebases. BoostBook takes 5% of cleared volume, which funds pokes and a MEZO buy-and-lock.

Size, honestly [I]:
- All veBTC fee income is ≈$11.7k/week, of which ≈10k is the sMUSD gauge's backlog-funded payout.
- Pricing a quarter of it would pay veMEZO ≈$150k/yr today, ≈10% of MEZO's market cap.
- That falls several-fold after the gauge cliff, unless new real yield (such as C1's) arrives.
- BoostBook's own fee is small. The value accrues to MEZO, a leadership pillar ('MEZO Gauges are the first step').

MEZO demand: a dollar yield on veMEZO makes locking rational, and VeMezoPool sellers who exit at 50% can rent instead.

Go-to-market:
1. Matchbox as a front end rather than a competitor.
2. Boar and Aurove as anchor buyers.
3. Enclave A, before #6114's lock ends on 2026-11-12 (it has no boost gauge).
4. sMUSD-gauge voters (225.8 units), where boost pays most, then the 1,796 veBTC holders and 1,376 veMEZO holders.
candidates.differentiation:
- Native addBribes and Matchbox (manual, off-chain profiles): pay-and-pray, with no price, no delivery guarantee and no refund; two deposits landed in three weeks. BoostBook adds price discovery, atomic vote-plus-bribe settlement, verified delivery and refunds, and can run behind Matchbox.
- Mezo's Pair & Boost: the buyer must buy and lock MEZO for up to four years. BoostBook rents per epoch with no MEZO exposure.
- BynD (prior winner, pooled veMEZO token), Aurove (liquid locker), Fractals, VeMezoPool: liquidity or pooling products. BoostBook issues no pooled token and concentrates no votes: each NFT votes only for orders it cleared, which answers the Earn whitepaper's warning about aggregators.
- Boar: a custodial managed-NFT relay, and a natural buyer.
- Mezoir (intent agent) and Lockwatch (expiry automation): neither prices boost or pays veMEZO in MUSD.
- The brief lists 'priced boost auctions' and 'non-custodial automation across Earn voters' as open whitespace. Neither is on Mezo's 2026 roadmap (veNFT marketplace, delegation, Simpler Earn), and native delegation would complement EarnAccounts.
candidates.testnet_feasibility:
Mostly yes, given a veMEZO float that we supply.
- Verified today: testnet U = 16.93 and M = 88.77M, so 5x on a 0.001 BTC max lock needs ≈5.2k veMEZO VP, and on 0.0001 BTC ≈520. Shorter locks need less, because u decays with time left. MUSD is whitelisted on testnet BoostVoter.
- Buyer path (≈3 minutes): 0.001 faucet BTC → createLock (the UI ends it next Thursday so u stays small) → createBoostGauge → instant fill from a reserve account, paid with dispenser MUSD → the explorer shows getBoost rising from 1e18 to 5e18 and the PoolsVoter weight updating.
- Seller path: 100 faucet MEZO → createLock → BoostAccount → ask → filled at the next settlement → claimBribes after Thursday. Earlier epochs' claims are pre-seeded for inspection.
- Thursday Nov 19 falls inside judging (Nov 16–22), so a live settlement and claim happen while judges are looking.

We must provide:
1. ≈60–100k test MEZO locked across ≈15 reserve and seller accounts, requested from Mezo DevRel (≈955M test MEZO sits in one address). Fallback: pooled faucet MEZO (100/day), enough for ≈2x demos on 0.001 BTC or 5x on 0.0001 BTC.
2. A MUSD dispenser for bids.
3. The settlement and re-poke keeper.

Limits: testnet sMUSD's gauge is not wired (vaultGauge = 0), so fee uplift shows as voting power and weight. We post weekly MUSD bribes on live testnet pool gauges (testnet PoolsVoter whitelists MUSD and MEZO) so boosted votes earn claimable rewards, and show the MUSD value on a mainnet fork.
candidates.mainnet_plan:
Wave 1 slice: BoostAccount, the createBoostGauge flow, a manually cleared settle() on testnet, and the price page.

Wave 2: immutable BoostAccount and EarnAccount implementations, the book, the oracle and the keeper on mainnet.
- Caps for the first four epochs: ≤2k MUSD escrowed per epoch, ≤200 MUSD per order, ≤20 lessees per epoch. Batches stay under the 10M gas limit and the 20-precompile limit.
- The team seeds ≈1M MEZO (≈$2.9k) of permanent veMEZO as initial supply and buys boost for team veBTC. Outreach to Boar, Aurove and Enclave A.
- Fork tests against live BoostVoter, VeBTC, VeMEZO and PoolsVoter: formula conformance, one-vote-per-epoch timing, the first-hour and vote-end windows, stale-boost enforcement.
- Invariants: no rent paid without a delivered vote; escrow conserved; failed settlement refunds; no code path moves an NFT except to its owner.
- An AI audit, verified source, and a public settlement ledger.
- Raise caps after 2–3 clean epochs.
candidates.key_risks:
1. The USD market is small and shrinking. Per-unit value is backlog-funded and falls ≈3–10x after ≈6–9 weeks [I], and boost is zero-sum among veBTC voters.
2. Concentration. Enclave #6033 already draws 40.85M veMEZO VP. If Enclave A boosts #6114 and votes the sMUSD gauge, per-unit rewards collapse.
3. Outside voters on buyer gauges can dilute the bribes.
4. Known BoostVoter issues: stale cached boosts, one veMEZO transiently backing several boosts (Thesis Defense #4), unbounded pokeBoosts (Halborn 7.8), and bribes lost on killed gauges (7.4).
5. Custody of 4-year veMEZO locks in clones: a bug could freeze them. Mitigated by immutability, per-NFT accounts, caps and an audit.
6. Timing edges: one vote per NFT per epoch, the first-hour DistributeWindow, and owners front-running settlement.
7. Upgradeable proxies, and scarce test MEZO.
8. It may be perceived as an aggregator or a rebuild of Matchbox or BynD. The answer is per-NFT accounts and on-chain price discovery.

candidates.name: Lockstep: borrow against veBTC without unlocking, settled at lock expiry instead of liquidated
candidates.one_liner: A permissionless retail counterpart to EnclaveDebtManager. Deposit a veBTC, keep it voting, and borrow MUSD at 50% LTV from an lsMUSD pool floored at the savings rate. Loans roll weekly with the lock, interest is paid from the NFT's own rewards, and a default ends with the lock's own expiry (≤28 days) plus an NFT auction, not an oracle liquidation.
candidates.problem:
veBTC is where Mezo's capital sits, and retail holders cannot borrow against it.
- veBTC holds 804.53 BTC (≈72% of the 1,117.1 BTC on Mezo) across 6,161 NFTs and 1,796 holders. The Enclaves hold 750.2 BTC and retail ≈54.3 BTC (≈$4.4M).
- Only the two Enclaves can borrow, through EnclaveDebtManager: 14.5M MUSD at 1%, ENCLAVE_ROLE-gated, at its mint cap, with no redemption or liquidation path.
- The docs FAQ says veBTC cannot be MUSD collateral (the whitepaper lists it as a future direction), and the Earn research found no veNFT lending product on Mezo.
- Retail exits are poor. Unlocking forfeits rewards and takes up to 28 days; selling means Vezo, or for veMEZO, VeMezoPool at 50%.
- Retail troves are gone (104 → 1), and BTC-backed borrowing on Mezo totals $66k, in the BTC/mUSDC market.
- Mezo's 28-day maximum lock makes settlement-by-expiry possible. Generic ve-lending (40 Acres, $3.62M) needs oracle liquidations of long locks [I].
candidates.mechanism:
Lock rules this relies on (verified in the VeBTC and PoolsVoter source by the input idea; voter timing re-verified today):
- lock end = floor((now + dur)/WEEK)·WEEK;
- increaseUnlockTime works only before expiry, on NORMAL, non-permanent locks;
- withdraw needs an expired, unvoted, NORMAL lock;
- voted NFTs can transfer, and their votes persist;
- vote and reset run once per epoch, never in its first hour;
- claims pay ownerOf.

1. Deposit. The borrower safeTransfers a NORMAL veBTC (VeBTC 0x3D4b…F279) to an immutable LockstepEscrow. The escrow reads locked(id) and escrowType(id) and rejects LOCKED and MANAGED NFTs. Permanent locks are accepted in 'call-on-notice' mode: a call resets the votes, then unlockPermanent restarts a 28-day countdown.
2. Credit limit = amount × Skip BTC/USD (0x7b7c…0015, ≤60 s) × LTV.
- LTV is 50% for rolling NORMAL locks and 40% for permanent locks, whose notice can run ≈35 days once epoch timing is included.
- Minimum 0.05 BTC per NFT on mainnet; lower in a labelled testnet pool.
3. Rolling. While a loan is in good standing, a permissionless keeper call has the escrow run VeBTC.increaseUnlockTime(id, 28 days) each epoch. That keeps voting power and rewards near maximum.
4. Self-repayment.
- As owner, the escrow votes PoolsVoter within the borrower's allowlist (default: the sMUSD vault gauge, whose FeesVotingReward 0x33b8… pays MUSD) and votes ValidatorsVoter, which is an independent vote.
- Each epoch it claims PoolsVoter.claimFeesAndBribes, ValidatorsVoter.claimBribes and the BTC chain-fee RewardsDistributor 0xb584….
- Rewards pay interest first, then principal; any surplus goes to the borrower.
- Optionally it buys boost through C2 when the expected return is positive.
5. Lenders. LockstepPool, an ERC-4626 ('lsMUSD'), keeps idle MUSD in sMUSD through wsMUSD, so its floor is the savings rate. The rate is set per epoch from a utilization curve. C1's vMUSD can allocate to it.
6. Call instead of liquidation. A missed interest payment, LTV above 65%, or the borrower's own request stops the extensions. Maturity then fixes at the current lock end (≤28 days away), and the borrower can repay any time before it.
7. Maturity.
- After epochStart + 1h, the escrow calls PoolsVoter.reset(id) and ValidatorsVoter.reset(id) (both are needed before withdraw), then VeBTC.withdraw(id), receiving native BTC through receive().
- The pool takes BTC worth the debt plus a 5% penalty and sells it through an oracle-anchored Dutch auction (B.AMM-style, or C1's backstop if built), never in one DEX dump. Surplus BTC goes to the borrower.
- On repayment the NFT goes back instead.
8. Emergency path. If collateral falls below 110% of debt during notice, a permissionless 24 h Dutch auction sells the NFT itself for MUSD, from 98% down to 85% of lockedBTC × price (from Bridgehead). The buyer gets what is effectively a BTC forward settling within 28 days. Proceeds repay lenders, and a junior reserve (10% of interest) absorbs any shortfall.
9. Phase 2, governance path. The same escrow becomes a LockstepMinter if Mezo adds it to the MUSD mint list, as it did for EnclaveDebtManager on 2026-04-28. Redemptions would be queued against maturing locks, giving MUSD a veBTC-backed redemption path that the Enclave route lacks.
10. Phase 2, USDC leg (from Bridgehead).
- Lenders on Base supply USDC to a CreditPool, and borrowers draw USDC on Base against the Mezo escrow, with credit limits relayed by Wormhole (reusing C4's relay).
- This avoids selling borrowed MUSD into a ≈$20k native bid.
- It is deferred because cross-chain credit attestation and message ordering are an XL build.

candidates.composable_outputs:
- lsMUSD: an ERC-4626 lender share with a savings-rate floor, backed by overcollateralised, short-dated BTC credit. It is an allocation target for C1's vMUSD.
- Loan positions as ERC-721s, each a claim on the debt plus the escrowed NFT, which lenders or a secondary desk can trade.
- A per-borrower ledger of repayments and votes: raw material for Luongo's 'votes as creditworthiness'.
- NFT Dutch-auction events: a new price signal for locked BTC.
- Escrow hooks for C2 boost purchases and Vezo listings.
candidates.business_model:
Who pays: veBTC borrowers pay MUSD interest weekly, mostly out of their own voting rewards. Defaulters pay a 5% penalty.

Who earns:
- lsMUSD lenders: the savings-rate floor plus a credit spread.
- A junior reserve: 10% of interest.
- The protocol: 10% of interest.
- Auction buyers: discounted BTC forwards.

MUSD demand: every loan is MUSD debt, i.e. structural future demand, and lenders park MUSD.

Sizing [I]: retail veBTC is ≈54 BTC (≈$4.4M). 30% uptake at 50% LTV is ≈$0.66M of MUSD credit, about 10x Mezo's whole Morpho loan book ($66k). The design also scales to Enclave-size NFTs.

Unit economics [I]:
- At 1x, 1 BTC voting the sMUSD gauge earns ≈44 MUSD/week today. A 50%-LTV loan at 4% costs ≈31 MUSD/week, so interest is covered now.
- After the gauge cliff (≈6–9 weeks), rewards fall to ≈4–15 MUSD/week. Self-repayment then becomes partial, unless the NFT is boosted (C2) or new real yield arrives.

Go-to-market:
1. veBTC holders via Matchbox and Vezo.
2. Boar and Aurove users who want liquidity without leaving their relays.
3. sMUSD holders as lenders.
4. Enclaves via Mezo Prime, for the minter path.
candidates.differentiation:
- Thaw (pipeline, not deployed): self-repaying credit against veBTC and veMEZO, plus a bot. Lockstep refuses veMEZO/MEZO collateral (a judge red flag at ≈$2.95M FDV), replaces oracle liquidations with expiry settlement, and rolls the lock so self-repayment does not decay.
- Latch (pipeline, one testnet cycle): peer-to-peer veBTC loans. Lockstep pools lenders behind a savings-rate floor, rolls automatically, and settles in kind or by NFT auction.
- Cosign (pipeline): MEZO-collateral Morpho cover, a different collateral.
- EnclaveDebtManager: institutions only, capped, no redemption path. Lockstep is its permissionless retail counterpart and proposes the redemption-backed minter Mezo could adopt.
- Lockwatch (submitted): automates expiry and can open a trove at expiry, which is not credit against a live lock.
- 40 Acres (Base/OP): long locks force oracle liquidations; Mezo's 28-day maximum removes that need.
- Vezo and VeMezoPool are exits, not credit.
candidates.governance_dependencies:
None for the core. The escrow owns the NFT, so transferFrom, vote, reset, claims, increaseUnlockTime, unlockPermanent and withdraw are all owner-level calls. Contracts may hold and vote veNFTs without an allowlist.

Phase 2 (optional): adding a LockstepMinter to the MUSD mint and burn lists needs multisig 0x98D8…7C7a, which has no timelock. This is the path EnclaveDebtManager took. Fallback: the core keeps lending existing MUSD from LockstepPool.

Hard constraints, not asks:
- split is team-gated, so NFTs are auctioned whole.
- Managed NFTs are governor-only and are not used.

Watch items:
- VeBTC and the voters are upgradeable proxies.
- The Oct-5 exploit came through ERC-2771 sender loss; Lockstep uses no forwarder (VeBTC.forwarder() = 0).
candidates.testnet_feasibility:

Judge path (≈5 minutes): 0.001 faucet BTC → createLock (the UI ends it on a Thursday) → deposit to the escrow → borrow ≈40 MUSD at 50% LTV → watch the escrow vote → repay with dispenser MUSD plus interest → NFT returned. Alternatively, request a roll and watch increaseUnlockTime.

Weekly cycles:
- Maturity, call and default run every Thursday on our own canary loans, with transaction hashes on an evidence page.
- Thursday Nov 19 falls inside judging, so a judge who opens a loan on Nov 16–18 sees it roll or mature live.
- The emergency NFT auction runs in a labelled demo pool with a guardian-set price; judges can trigger it and bid with dispenser MUSD.

Caveat: testnet sMUSD's gauge is not wired (vaultGauge = 0, re-read today), and testnet PoolsVoter whitelists only MUSD and MEZO. On testnet the escrow therefore votes a live pool gauge on which we post weekly MUSD bribes, so the claim → repay loop is real. sMUSD-gauge MUSD is shown on a mainnet fork.

We provide ≈25k test MUSD to seed lsMUSD (from a Mezo DevRel grant; fallback: pooled faucet BTC swapped on the testnet MUSD/BTC pool), the dispenser, and the keeper.
candidates.mainnet_plan:
Wave 1 slice: escrow deposit, borrow and repay on testnet, with fork tests of VeBTC transfer, vote and increaseUnlockTime.

Wave 2: the immutable escrow, pool and keeper on mainnet.
- Caps: ≤0.5 BTC collateral per loan; lsMUSD ≤25k MUSD; LTV 50% (40% for permanent locks); ≤10 concurrent loans. The team seeds lenders and opens the first loans with team veBTC.
- Fork tests against live VeBTC, PoolsVoter and ValidatorsVoter: epoch windows, reset-then-withdraw, rolling, permanent-lock calls, claims paid to ownerOf.
- Invariants: debt never exceeds the claim on BTC; no NFT leaves the escrow except on repayment, settlement or auction; reserve accounting is conserved.
- An AI audit with a findings ledger, verified source, and a public loan ledger.

Phase 2: a LockstepMinter design document and fork-tested code for Mezo; the Base USDC leg once C4's relay exists.
candidates.key_risks:
1. The retail market is small (≈54 BTC; the average NFT is ≈0.009 BTC), and the Enclaves may never use it.
2. Price risk during notice. A BTC drawdown above ≈45–50% inside a ≤28-day window creates bad debt (March 2020 fell ≈50% in days). Mitigated by the emergency auction, the junior reserve, and lower LTV on permanent locks.
3. Self-repayment depends on gauge payouts that fall several-fold after the backlog drains, and on Enclave votes diluting rewards.
4. Epoch timing: reset works only after epochStart + 1h, there is one vote per epoch, and both voters must be reset before withdraw.
5. Settlement BTC still needs buyers in ≈$55k of MUSD-side depth.
6. Contested category: Thaw, Latch and Cosign may land first.
7. A full loan cycle takes up to a week, so judges see live maturities only around Thursdays.
8. VeBTC and the voters are upgradeable proxies.
candidates.wow_moment: A judge borrows MUSD against a veBTC they created two minutes earlier. The loan card reads 'Maturity = your lock expiry (Thu 00:00 UTC) · Liquidation bot: none'. Then the escrow's weekly claim lands voting rewards that visibly shrink the debt: Mezo's own vote-escrow is paying off the loan.

candidates.problem:
MUSD holders who need dollars must sell into a bid that barely exists, and nothing lets them borrow instead.
- No working MUSD-collateral market exists. Ethereum Morpho MUSD/USDT (91.5%) holds $0, and its oracle reverts with StalePrice. Morpho lists no MUSD market on Base, and Ethereum's MUSD-loan markets hold ≈$100 [ideator RL].
- No working MUSD/USD oracle exists off Mezo:
  - Base Pyth has no pushed MUSD price (PriceFeedNotFound, reported by two inputs).
  - Ethereum's last update was 2026-07-16, at $1.00296.
  - Public Hermes now answers HTTP 401 'unauthorized' for MUSD and BTC update data, even though the feed is listed as Crypto.MEZO.MUSD/USD (re-checked read-only today).
  - Only Mezo's Pyth Core Compatible 0x5D28… is fresh.
- Exit liquidity is a cliff:
  - Mezo's CL10 pool holds 5.33M MUSD against 9,740 mUSDC (re-read today);
  - 10k MUSD sells for 9,485 mUSDC;
  - 100k on Curve costs ≈4%;
  - the USDC bid across Mezo, Base and Ethereum is ≈$0.38M against 29.48M MUSD.
- Base holds 1.016M MUSD, 927.4k of it in Aero CL10 beside 227.8k USDC, with no lending use. Meanwhile ≈$950M of Base USDC sits in Morpho vaults at 3.5–4.7%.
- Mezo's roadmap asks for MUSD 'as collateral… in external lending markets', Base first. Track 1 lists cross-chain lending, and 0 of 40 submissions deploy on Base or Ethereum.
candidates.mechanism:
1. MusdPriceEmitter (Mezo, immutable).
- It reads Pyth Core Compatible 0x5D28… getPriceNoOlderThan(MUSD 0x0617…c6de, 3,900 s), pushed by Mezo's own pusher so no Hermes access is needed, and the 30-minute TWAP of the Tigris mUSDC/MUSD CL10 pool 0xCC37… via observe([1800, 0]).
- It refuses to publish if the two differ by more than 1%. Otherwise it publishes (seq, price, conf, publishTime, twapTick) with Wormhole core 0xaBf8…0Da8 publishMessage (messageFee 0).
- poke() is permissionless.
2. MusdOracle (Base, immutable; Morpho IOracle and Chainlink AggregatorV3).
- update(vaa) verifies through Base Wormhole core 0xbebd…8ac6 parseAndVerifyVM, and requires emitterChain 50, our emitter and a strictly increasing seq.
- price = min(relayed Pyth, Aero CL10 0xb02F… 30-minute TWAP, 1.0) × (1 − 0.5%).
- It never reverts on divergence (it uses the lower fresh source, so liquidations keep working) and reverts only if every source is staler than 6 h.
- If the Aero pool migrates, we deploy a new oracle and market and the curated vault reallocates. No oracle gets an admin path.
- If a Hermes API key is obtained, a Base Pyth pull update becomes a third source [U].
3. Markets on Base Morpho Blue 0xBBBB…FFCb: collateral MUSD (same address on Base), loan USDC 0x8335…2913, AdaptiveCurveIrm 0x4641…2687, LLTV 0.86 (enabled). A 0.915 twin opens after evidence.
4. Curated vault: 'Portside USDC', from the MetaMorpho v1.1 factory 0xFf62…5918 on Base.
- It supplies only these markets.
- Absolute caps are scripted to ≤25% of Aero USDC within 1% of spot. Cap increases wait 3 days, and the guardian can only lower caps.
- A 10% performance fee goes to a FeeRouter.
5. One click from Mezo.
- PortsideGateway.openOnBase(amount, borrowUsdc, maxLtvBps, deadline, permit, intentSig) pulls MUSD by permit and calls NttManagerWithExecutor 0x484b… transfer(nttManager 0x7efb…, amount, 30, recipient = the user's CREATE2 PositionProxy on Base, …). This is the path that carries Mezo's NTT traffic (11,725 mainnet txs; a sample Mezo→Base delivery took 14 s).
- It also publishes the signed EIP-712 intent as a Wormhole message.
- On Base, PortsideExecutor.execute(intentVaa) checks that the MUSD reached the proxy, then calls supplyCollateral and borrow(onBehalf = proxy, receiver = user) within the user's maxLtv (UI default: 75% of LLTV).
- Repay and withdraw happen on Base, sponsored by EIP-712 if needed. closeToMezo() repays, withdraws, and returns the MUSD over NTT (16–22 minutes, set by Base finality).
6. Liquidations. Morpho.liquidate is permissionless. Our bot is the backstop: it sells seized MUSD on Aero, or routes it to Mezo (or into C6's bid) when Base depth is thin.
7. Fee loop. The FeeRouter swaps USDC→MUSD on Aero (buy pressure), sends it to Mezo over NTT, and calls sMUSD.receiveProtocolYield (permissionless). ≈72% of that accrues to VaultGauge 0x6778… and reaches veBTC voters through FeesVotingReward 0x33b8….
8. Second collateral (if C5 is built): the fMUSD savings receipt, with oracle = convertToAssets × MusdOracle.
9. Ethereum spoke: the same oracle and a 91.5% market (enabled there), replacing the dead MUSD/USDT market.

candidates.business_model:
Who pays:

Who earns:

- The curator takes 10%; half goes to sMUSD via receiveProtocolYield and on to veBTC voters.
- Executors are reimbursed.

MUSD demand:
- MUSD becomes money you can borrow against, so holders raise USDC without dumping into Mezo's bid of ≈8–10k.
- The FeeRouter buys MUSD on Aero.
- Collateral posted on Base takes MUSD out of circulation.

Target users:
1. veBTC voters receiving 10k MUSD/week today.
2. Base MUSD LPs (927k in Aero).
3. Large holders. Enclave A owes 10.5M MUSD and keeps a 5.26M single-sided sell range; Portside lets holders like this borrow instead of selling, at whatever scale exit depth allows.
4. Base USDC lenders, reached through Morpho's UIs and aggregators.

Honest: paying ≈4.5%+ for USDC against a 0%-yield asset suits liquidity needs, not carry trades, so early volume will be small.
candidates.differentiation:

It uses unmodified Morpho Blue on Base mainnet and canonical NTT MUSD, so its new attack surface is one small oracle and a gateway.
- Ditto dMUSD converts MUSD into Spark USDS (convertToAssets ≈0.981), so depositors already took the discount. Portside keeps MUSD exposure and still delivers USDC.

- Prior art exists, but none of it is on Base and none has a working oracle: the dead Ethereum MUSD/USDT market, and a dormant third-party testnet Morpho 0x6F1a… with ≈40 MUSD-loan markets.

candidates.mechanism:
1. FerryVault on Base: an ERC-4626 over MUSD (same address on Base), with ERC-7540 async redeem. It accounts in internal buckets, not balanceOf, so donations cannot move the price:
- a Base MUSD buffer (target 20%);
- remotePrincipal (MUSD held in sMUSD on Mezo for the vault);
- inFlight;
- yield received.
2. push() is permissionless and bounded. It sends excess buffer through the Base NttManager 0x3EB4…1Bc1 (burning) with transfer(amount, 50, FerryHub, …). The Mezo manager 0x7efb… unlocks it to the hub, and inFlight tracks the transfer.
3. FerryHub on Mezo deposits into sMUSD 0xb4D4…, directly or through C1's wsMUSD, and records remotePrincipal. It stays unstaked, so the MUSD yield stays with savers.
4. Oracle-free yield (from Harbor's mechanism lens).
- Weekly, the hub calls PCV.distributeMUSD(), then sMUSD.claimYield(), and bridges only the yield to FerryVault through NttManagerWithExecutor 0x484b… (≈14 s Mezo→Base).
- sMUSD principal is strictly 1:1 (there is no exchange rate), so remote principal never changes value.
- totalAssets = buffer + remotePrincipal + inFlight + yield received. The share price rises only when real MUSD lands, and it is monotone. This uses the very quirk that makes sMUSD hard to integrate.
5. Proof of reserves (from Ferry and Outpost).
- The hub publishes (sMUSD balance, remotePrincipal, received NTT sequence numbers, nonce) with Wormhole core 0xaBf8… publishMessage (fee 0).
- FerryVault.receiveReport(vaa) verifies it on Base core 0xbebd… (emitter chain 50, our emitter, increasing sequence), reconciles inFlight, and bounds each streamed yield amount by maxAPR × Δt.
- If the reported balance falls below remotePrincipal, deposits pause and the price is marked down until reconciled.
6. Withdrawals are instant from the buffer. Larger ones become ERC-7540 requests: the vault publishes a Base Wormhole message; the hub verifies it with the Mezo core's parseAndVerifyVM, calls sMUSD.withdraw (which auto-claims), and returns the MUSD over NTT. Claims settle after ≈20–25 minutes, set by Base finality on the request leg.
7. Zap: USDC → MUSD on Aero with peg and slippage bounds, so depositors buy below peg.
8. Collateral. fMUSD lists as a second collateral in C4's Base Morpho market family, with oracle = convertToAssets × C4's relayed MusdOracle. Base Pyth cannot price it today (no MUSD feed on Base; Hermes 401), so a Ferry-only build still uses C4's emitter for any USD mark.
9. Optional MEZO Gauge. Mezo already routes veMEZO-voted MEZO to Aero through ThirdPartyVoter and RemoteGaugeRegistry 0x8236…; a gauge for Ferry depositors is the governance ask.

Dropped from Outpost: a separate wsMUSD NTT token and PSM. It meant a second bridge configuration, fragmented liquidity, and a canonical-token question for Mezo. Its rate-relay bounds survive in step 5.

candidates.mechanism:
Mezo leg (core):
1. ParVault: an ERC-4626 over mUSDC 0x0467…c197 (share: parUSDC).
- Deposits are priced at a NAV built from a 30-minute pool TWAP (CLPool.observe, after increaseObservationCardinalityNext). They revert if spot deviates from the TWAP by more than 0.3%.
- MUSD inventory is marked at min(1, Pyth MUSD no older than 3,900 s on 0x5D28…/0x933a…, TWAP).
- Withdrawals are in kind and pro rata: idle mUSDC, a slice of every position (via NFPM decreaseLiquidity/collect), and wsMUSD. Exits therefore need no oracle and can never be paused.
- An optional single-asset exit swaps the MUSD leg with a minimum-out guard.
2. Bid ladder.
- A permissionless, bounded rebalance() derives 8 tranches deterministically from the TWAP tick, so the keeper chooses no prices.
- The tranches are single-sided mUSDC ranges just above the current tick (token0 is mUSDC, token1 is MUSD). Today that is ticks 276430–276510, i.e. MUSD from ≈$0.9893 down to ≈$0.981.
- One small two-sided straddle sits at the current tick so the vault stays in range.
- Positions are minted with NFPM 0x509B…874c mint(tickSpacing 10) in CL10 0xCC37…aC1a, and staked in gauge 0x6d44…Fc57 with deposit(tokenId) to earn MEZO.
3. Fills are automatic. Every seller who crosses the pool hits Par's bids, whether through CLSwapRouter, an aggregator, a zap or another protocol, with no integration.
4. sweep().
- Once a tranche has been fully crossed for 30 minutes, the vault unstakes it (gauge.withdraw), collects the MUSD, and deposits it into wsMUSD over sMUSD, so inventory earns the savings rate.
- MEZO from gauge.getReward(tokenId) reaches parUSDC holders through a reward-per-share accumulator. Holders can claim it or auto-lock it with VeMEZO createLockFor.
5. On-chain limits.
- Inventory ≤50% of NAV, plus per-tranche and total caps.
- A depeg breaker stops new bids and pulls unfilled tranches when Pyth MUSD < 0.97, the TWAP < 0.97, or the tick moves more than 100 in an hour.
- A 2-of-3 Safe guardian can pause deposits and new bids only.
- There is no admin withdrawal and no upgradeable proxy.
6. Inventory exits.
- Single-sided asks just under Enclave A's wall (≈0.990–0.991), placed when the TWAP ≥ average cost + 0.2%.
- A redemption-arbitrage module calls TroveManager.redeemCollateral (hints from HintHelpers.getRedemptionHints and SortedTroves.findInsertPosition) only when capacity exists, Pyth MUSD < 0.9925 and TCR ≥ MCR. It sells the BTC back on CL200 only if the round trip clears a minimum profit. With ≈12.5k of capacity today it is mostly dormant.
- Otherwise, inventory is held in wsMUSD.

Base leg (Wave 2):
7. TideVault on Base: an ERC-4626 over USDC.
- 80–90% of USDC sits idle in a whitelisted Base Morpho USDC vault (Spark 0x7BfA… at 4.24%, or Gauntlet USDC Prime 0xeE8F… at 4.72%); 10–20% is a buffer.
- An oracle-anchored RFQ quotes sellMusd at P_bid = min(C4's relayed Mezo Pyth price, Aero CL10 TWAP, Tigris CL10 TWAP, 1.0) × (1 − spread). The spread widens with inventory, from 0.4% to 1.5%.
- Per-block and per-epoch caps apply. Buying halts below 0.97 or when sources diverge by more than 1.5%.
- Inventory is capped at 30% of NAV. Above a threshold, a keeper sends MUSD over NTT to C5's hub on Mezo, into sMUSD, and recalls it when price ≥ 0.995. buyMusd sells inventory back at max(oracle, 0.995) × (1 + fee).
- NAV marks MUSD at min(oracle, TWAPs). When the buffer is short, withdrawals pay in kind, so the vault never fire-sells.
- Base Pyth cannot price MUSD (there is no feed on Base, and Hermes returns 401), hence the relayed price.
8. 'Sell where the bid is' router on Mezo.
- It compares QuoterV2 quotes with Router.getAmountsOut (Route[]).
- If Mezo pools cannot meet minOut, it sends the MUSD through NttManagerWithExecutor (≈14 s) to a per-intent CREATE2 executor on Base, along with a signed Wormhole intent (C4's pattern).
- The executor sells into TideVault or Aero and pays USDC on Base, or refunds the MUSD on Base if minOut fails.

Shared:
9. PegLens, a view contract and public page, shows:
- the MUSD price (Pyth and TWAP);
- stablecoin bid depth within 0.5/1/2% (QuoterV2, plus getAmountOut on the sAMM and MUSD/mUSDT);
- live redemption capacity, by walking SortedTroves from getLast with TroveManager.getCurrentICR;
- the size of Enclave A's wall;
- Par's fills, with each seller's price improvement against a fork-simulated no-Par counterfactual.
10. Fees: 10% of realized PnL and of MEZO, plus 5 bps on routed volume. Part is donated to sMUSD via receiveProtocolYield.

candidates.composable_outputs:
- parUSDC and tUSDC: ERC-4626 shares over a bounded book of USDC plus discounted MUSD held in sMUSD, usable later as collateral or as LP assets.
- The bid itself lives in the canonical pool, so every router, aggregator, zap, liquidator and arbitrageur on Mezo gets depth without integrating anything.
- An on-chain RFQ interface on Base (quoteBuy/sellMusd/quoteSell/buyMusd) that routers and liquidators, including C4's, can call.
- PegLens: an on-chain and HTTP feed of MUSD price, bid depth at ±0.5/1/2%, live redemption capacity and the wall size, usable by oracle sentinels, dashboards and Mezo itself.

candidates.business_model:
Who pays:
- MUSD sellers pay the bid's spread, 0.02–1.0% below TWAP. That is still far better than today, when Mezo's bid ends near 10k MUSD and the sAMM pays 963.4 per 1,000.
- Routed volume pays 5 bps.

Who earns:
- Depositors earn spread capture when inventory exits, roughly the sMUSD rate on inventory, and MEZO from the CL10 gauge (≈355k MEZO/week goes to in-range staked liquidity). On Base they also earn the 4.2–4.7% Morpho USDC base yield on idle cash.
- Par takes 10% of realized PnL and of MEZO; sMUSD gets a fee share.

MUSD demand: a standing, transparent, funded buyer up to the caps, with inventory parked productively, makes MUSD safer to hold.

Honest returns:
- Enclave A's wall caps the upside near $0.991, so spread capture is 0.2–0.4%.
- MEZO is illiquid on-chain (MEZO/MUSD is ≈1.4k MUSD deep), so the headline APY counts MEZO at zero.
- The Base leg's base yield is what makes the bid cheap to hold.

Go-to-market:
1. Mezo-aligned capital and market makers first.
2. Base USDC depositors, who give up little versus Spark or Gauntlet.
3. Aero LPs already carrying MUSD risk.
4. 'Sell on Base' inside Mezo-side UIs.
5. A MEZO Gauge ask.
It pairs with C4 as that candidate's liquidation backstop.
candidates.differentiation:
- Mezo's SafetyBuffer (an owner-only redemption absorber) is closed by redemption, and redemption bots extract from capacity that is now ≈12.5k.
- Pylon's redemption shield, Lifeline and Vigil protect borrowers; none of them buys MUSD.
- Range is a generic two-sided CL rebalancer: not peg-aware, no breaker, no sMUSD inventory, no redemption leg.
- mbLP and MezoRoute borrow MUSD to LP it, adding supply to the ask side, the opposite of what the peg needs.
- MEZO Gauges and Matchbox pay LPs on other chains whose USDC side is thin; Par funds the bid itself.
- B.AMM (thUSD BAMM.sol, MIT) inspired the oracle-anchored pricing, but it sells BTC out of a Stability Pool.
- Andre's critique that a USDC off-ramp 'doesn't really do anything' does not apply: this is market structure that improves every swap and parks the MUSD it buys productively.
- No submission or pipeline project funds a USDC bid, and none is on Base.

candidates.name: Sigil: passkey Safes on Mezo that pay gas in MUSD, reachable from Base
candidates.one_liner: Face ID creates a real Safe on Mezo. Mezo's P256VERIFY precompile checks its signatures, and its gas is refunded in MUSD. One tap saves in sMUSD, borrows against BTC, pays a name.mezo, locks MEZO or rescues stranded BTC. Base users can send MUSD or MEZO straight to the same counterfactual Safe and act on arrival.
candidates.problem:
Getting to MUSD and MEZO now takes an EVM wallet, a seed phrase and BTC for gas before the first action.
- Native BTC bridge-in closed 2026-10-13, and BTC-wallet sign-up is being sunset.
- Mezo has no working account abstraction. EntryPoint v0.7 has 0 transactions, and there is no bundler or paymaster. Meta-transactions have been 'disabled altogether' since the 2026-10-05 exploit (5.52 BTC).
- Passport/OrangeKit Safes cannot sign MUSD permits or trove signatures (ECDSA-only, no EIP-1271), and Mezo's relayer refunds itself in BTC. Get Gas only swaps into a fixed 0.0001 BTC.
- Discovery is broken. 5.70 BTC (≈$459k) of redemption surplus sits unclaimed across 27 accounts, 10 of them above 0.1 BTC, and the owners don't know.
- Off-Mezo holders are stranded. 1.016M MUSD on Base, 608.8k on Ethereum, and ≈292M MEZO on Base cannot reach sMUSD, veMEZO, boost or MEZO-Gauge votes without four steps: bridging, a Mezo wallet, BTC for gas, and (on testnet) a manual redeem. NTT delivers tokens but triggers no action on arrival.
- Track 2 asks how to make MUSD and MEZO easier to discover, access and use, and the roadmap names 'A Simpler Earn Experience'.
candidates.mechanism:
1. Account: a Safe 1.4.1, owned by a WebAuthn signer.
- Built from SafeL2 0x29fc…0C762 via ProxyFactory 0x4e1D…ec67 createProxyWithNonce, with CompatibilityFallbackHandler 0xfd07…Ec99. All are live on both networks.
- The signer comes from Safe's passkey modules (SafeWebAuthnSignerFactory and SignerProxy, LGPL-3.0). They are not yet on Mezo, so we deploy them deterministically through the Safe singleton factory 0x914d…43d7.
- Signatures verify through Mezo's P256VERIFY precompile at 0x…0100 (a valid secp256r1 signature returns 1 on mainnet and testnet), with FCL as the fallback verifier.
- The address is counterfactual from the passkey's (x, y) and a salt; the first deployment is sponsored.
2. Relaying without meta-transactions.
- Our open-source relayer calls Safe.execTransaction(…, gasToken = MUSD, refundReceiver = relayer, signatures). This is the pattern Mezo's OrangeKit relayer already uses, which refunds in BTC instead.
- The passkey signs the SafeTx hash, which includes gasPrice and gasToken, so the refund can never exceed what the user approved.
- Quotes are computed off-chain from Skip BTC/USD and the chain gas price (≈1.46e6 wei on mainnet; cents per action).
- msg.sender to every protocol is the Safe; there is no ERC-2771.
3. One-signature actions, batched as approve + action through MultiSendCallOnly 0x9641…02e2. No permits are needed, which sidesteps the Safe/permit limitation.
- Save: sMUSD deposit/withdraw/claimYield.
- Borrow: Morpho's BTC/mUSDC market 0x6f88… or C1's BTC→MUSD market; or a Safe-owned trove via BorrowerOperations (the Safe has receive()).
- Pay: MUSD to an address or to a name.mezo, resolved server-side via GET api.mezo.org/accounts/{name}.mezo and shown before signing.
- Earn: VeMEZO createLock, VeBTC createLock; votes through C2's EarnAccount if it is built.
4. Discover and rescue.
- A scanner reads CollSurplusPool.getCollateral, sMUSD claimableYield and expired veBTC locks (VeBTC.locked) for any address.
- An EOA owner signs an EIP-712 ClaimCollateral, and the relayer calls claimCollateralWithSignature(borrower, recipient = their Sigil Safe, sig, deadline): a gasless rescue.
- One more tap deploys the BTC into sMUSD or Morpho.
5. Reach from Base (from Inbox).
- The Safe address is predictable before it exists, so a Base user can send MUSD or MEZO to it over NTT.
- A sponsored Base helper takes a token permit (MUSD and MEZO on Base expose DOMAIN_SEPARATOR) and calls the MUSD manager 0x3EB4…, or the MEZO NTT peer of hub 0x5E66…, with the Safe as recipient.
- On arrival, the relayer executes the user's passkey-signed SafeTx: save; lock MEZO with VeMEZO.createLockFor straight to the user; vote or bribe through BoostVoter or ThirdPartyVoter; or repay a trove. It is refunded from the arriving asset, so the user never holds BTC.
6. Express fills (Wave 2 stretch).
- Base→Mezo takes 16–22 minutes for finality.
- A capped solver that has seen N Base blocks fronts the asset on Mezo and executes immediately. It is repaid by a per-intent CREATE2 settlement address (salt = intentHash) when the NTT leg lands.
- With no solver, the intent simply executes on arrival.
7. Recovery and portability.
- Add a second device's passkey, or an EOA co-owner (addOwnerWithThreshold).
- Because it is a plain Safe, an EOA co-owner can operate it from safe.mezo.org if our relayer or app disappears.
8. SDK: @sigil/mezo (TypeScript) plus a RainbowKit connector. Passport is a RainbowKit wrapper, so Passport dApps can add 'Continue with passkey' and MUSD gas in a few lines.

Corrections to the inputs:
- A Coinbase Smart Wallet passkey is bound to Coinbase's rpId, so reusing it on Mezo is unlikely [I]. The design only needs the Base wallet (any wallet) to send to the Sigil address.
- Whether P256VERIFY counts toward the 20-precompile limit is unverified, so batches are budgeted as if it does.

- Standard Safe accounts: every Mezo protocol sees a normal msg.sender, and Safe tooling works.

candidates.business_model:
Who pays:
- Users pay gas in MUSD with a small markup (cents per action).
- dApps pay, through the SDK, for sponsored onboarding (the first deployment plus N actions). This is the main B2B line.
- Base arrivals pay an executor fee (10 bps, minimum 0.25 MUSD, capped by the user's maxFee); express fills pay 5–15 bps.

Who earns: the relayer and solver operators. Mezo gains users who never need BTC to start.

MUSD and MEZO demand:
- Every account holds MUSD for gas.
- One tap routes the ≈1.6M MUSD on Base and Ethereum into sMUSD, and off-Mezo MEZO into veMEZO locks (only 280.69M MEZO is locked today).

Go-to-market:
1. Offer Sigil as Passport's passkey option, replacing the sunset BTC-wallet path.
2. Integrations with Matchbox, Mezo Market and other apps.
3. The 27 surplus accounts, via the scanner.
4. Base MUSD and MEZO holders.
5. Ignition explicitly lists developer tooling and SDKs.

Honest: per-transaction revenue on Mezo is tiny, and Base MEZO is concentrated (one EOA holds 77.8M), so this is a B2B-plus-grants business.
candidates.differentiation:
- Mezo Passport/OrangeKit: Bitcoin-wallet signers (being sunset), Safes that cannot use MUSD permits or trove signatures, and BTC refunds. Sigil reuses the same Safe-plus-relayer pattern with passkeys and MUSD refunds, and ships as a Passport connector.
- Pocket (submitted): Privy social login, i.e. third-party key infrastructure. Sigil's keys live in the device's secure enclave.
- Kudi, MUSD Pocket, the PayLinks: front ends on EOAs that still need BTC for gas.
- Get Gas (a fixed 0.0001 BTC); the x402 facilitator (sponsors transfers only); Mezo Agent Toolkit and the x402 entries (built for agents, not people).
- Mezo's NttManagerWithExecutor moves tokens but executes nothing; Mezo Flow only pitches cross-chain.
- Prior winners MezoPay, SuperPage and Cark are payment and savings apps on EOAs.
- No entry uses P256VERIFY, passkeys, MUSD-denominated gas, or execution on arrival from Base.
candidates.governance_dependencies:
None. Safe 1.4.1, the singleton factory, the P256 precompile, sMUSD, Morpho, BorrowerOperationsSignatures, VeMEZO, BoostVoter and NTT sends are all usable permissionlessly.

Optional:
- Mezo adopts the connector inside Passport. This is a product decision, not a multisig action.
- Mezo documents the Mezo ID API and its CORS policy. Fallback: server-side resolution that shows the address.

Constraints:
- Bribes need whitelisted tokens. MUSD and MEZO are whitelisted on mainnet; testnet ThirdPartyVoter whitelists none, so MEZO-Gauge bribes are shown on a fork only.
- NTT rate limits and pausing belong to multisig 0x98D8…7C7a.

Nothing relies on MezoForwarder or meta-transactions.
candidates.testnet_feasibility:
Judges need only a phone or laptop with passkeys; no faucet visit.

We must provide:
1. Safe's passkey contracts deployed on testnet.
2. A relayer funded with ≈0.01 testnet BTC (thousands of transactions at ≈146 wei gas).
3. A Judge Kit per new account, gated by Turnstile on the relayer: 50 test MUSD, 0.0005 test BTC for collateral and 20 test MEZO. MUSD comes from a DevRel grant or team troves; MEZO from faucet drips or a request (≈955M test MEZO sits in one address).
4. For the Base path: Base Sepolia MUSD and MEZO dispensers (Base Sepolia MEZO supply is only 786, so we bridge team inventory), a redeemer bot for testnet NTT, a sponsored Base sender, and a solver float on Mezo testnet for express fills.

Judge path (≈5 minutes):
1. Face ID; the Safe deploys (explorer link).
2. Claim the kit.
3. Save 30 MUSD in testnet sMUSD, paying gas in MUSD.
4. Pay a name.mezo (via api.test.mezo.org).
5. Lock 20 MEZO into veMEZO.
6. Supply 0.0005 BTC and borrow a few mUSDC on testnet Morpho (its vault holds ≈33k mUSDC).
7. Add a second device's passkey.
8. Scan any address for unclaimed value.
9. From Base Sepolia, send MEZO and watch it arrive locked as veMEZO (express), or tracked over ≈20 minutes (non-express).

Not judge-testable: rescuing their own CollSurplusPool BTC, since judges have none. The scanner works on any address, and the gasless rescue is shown on a mainnet fork.

Wave 1 slice: passkey Safe creation on testnet, the MUSD-refund relayer, and sMUSD save/withdraw, with fork tests.

Wave 2: borrow, pay (Mezo ID), veMEZO lock, recovery, the scanner and gasless rescue, the SDK and connector; then the Base arrival path and express fills; an AI audit and threat model; the evidence page.
- Mainnet: deploy the passkey contracts through the singleton factory. Relayer budget 0.002 BTC/day with per-account daily caps. Only the first deployment is sponsored; refunds are in MUSD from day one. A UI balance cap (for example 1k MUSD) applies until a third-party audit.
- Base helpers are immutable, with per-intent caps (5k MUSD, 2M MEZO), a 50k MUSD daily cap and a 5k solver float.
- Testing: fork tests run passkey → Safe → sMUSD/Morpho on mainnet state; an invariant fuzz proves the refund never exceeds the signed maximum; cross-chain signature-domain fuzzing for replay; a test enforcing the precompile budget.
- The evidence page shows accounts created, every relayed transaction with its MUSD refund, sMUSD deposits, P256 verification gas, and Base→Mezo transaction pairs.

After the hackathon: a Passport integration proposal, a third-party audit of the relayer, SDK and Base helpers, and an Ignition grant.
candidates.key_risks:
1. Wallets are the highest-stakes category, and loss of funds is fatal. Mitigations: audited Safe and passkey code, multi-device passkeys plus an EOA recovery owner, and per-account caps until audit.
2. Passkeys are bound to our domain (rpId), so setting up recovery is part of onboarding.
3. Relayer or solver liveness and censorship. Users can always self-submit execTransaction with BTC gas through Safe tooling.
4. Judges may score a wallet as surface integration. It must visibly drive deep actions: sMUSD, Morpho, troves, veMEZO, the CollSurplusPool rescue, NTT arrivals.
5. It may look like a rebuild of Passport; it is framed as a Passport connector.
6. The Base path adds cross-chain signature-domain or replay bugs and Base→Mezo latency. Express fills move reorg and queueing risk onto our capped solver.
7. Track 2 is crowded with consumer and payment apps, and the Mezo ID API is undocumented.
8. Unverified: whether P256VERIFY counts toward the 20-precompile limit, and whether the x402 facilitator accepts EIP-1271 signatures.
candidates.wow_moment: From a fresh phone with no wallet, no seed phrase and no BTC: Face ID creates a real Safe on Mezo in ≈3 s. Then 30 MUSD goes into sMUSD, 5 MUSD to a name.mezo and 20 MEZO into veMEZO, all in ≈60 s, with Mezo's own P256 precompile verifying every signature and gas paid in MUSD in each transaction. Then, from Base Sepolia, one passkey tap sends MEZO that appears on Mezo already locked as veMEZO in the judge's name.

candidates.merged_from: Tab. It takes Harbor's (judge lens) per-user BorrowAccount pattern for isolation, and shares its market with C1 if both are built.
candidates.name: Tab: capped, revocable BTC-backed MUSD credit lines for apps, agents and cards
candidates.one_liner: Post BTC once, then grant apps, AI agents or card processors capped, rate-limited, revocable rights to draw MUSD to an allowed recipient from a redemption-free Morpho position. There is no 2,000-MUSD minimum and no code path to the collateral.
candidates.problem:
Every MUSD payment product assumes the payer already holds MUSD, and getting MUSD is the hard part.
- A trove needs ≥1,800 MUSD of net debt (2,000 with the gas reserve, ≈0.027 BTC). The faucet gives 0.001 BTC, and most payments are far smaller. Mezo's own unmerged Microloans.sol shows the gap is known.
- While MUSD trades below the ≈$0.9925 floor, any new mainnet trove is first in the redemption queue (1 trove left; 681 redemptions in ≈30 days).
- Native delegation (BorrowerOperationsSignatures) is ECDSA-only with one sequential nonce per borrower, so only one authorization can be outstanding. It has no caps, periods or price conditions, and Passport Safes cannot sign it.
- Morpho's setAuthorization is all-or-nothing: an authorized address can borrow the maximum and withdraw collateral.
- Mezo's roadmap names cards and 'payment rails for AI agents'. x402 works on Mezo, but its mainnet facilitator signer has sent 22 transactions.
- Payments are saturated (13+ entries) and x402/agents has 6, but none of them supplies credit.
candidates.mechanism:
1. Market. The MUSD-loan / BTC-collateral market on Morpho 0x5658… (AdaptiveCurveIrm 0x3760…, LLTV 0.86; testnet 0xCe1d…, 0x0c97…, 0.77), created permissionlessly, or C1's M1 if it exists.
- Oracle: Skip BTC/USD with a 60 s staleness revert, divided by max(1, Pyth MUSD).
- Liquidity comes from a Vault V2 (VaultV2Factory 0xA64f…; configuration only, no new code), with idle MUSD in sMUSD.
2. TabAccount: a per-user EIP-1167 clone of one immutable implementation, which owns that user's Morpho position.
- No singleton ever holds Morpho authorization over every user. This replaces the input's TabCredit design, where a single contract held setAuthorization over all positions, so one bug would hit every user.
- depositCollateral() is payable. Native BTC is also the ERC-20 at 0x7b7C…0000, so the clone approves Morpho and calls supplyCollateral(onBehalf = clone).
3. Allowances: approveCredit(spender, {maxOutstanding, periodLimit, period, maxLtvBps, expiry, recipientLock}), or approveCreditWithSig, which verifies ECDSA or EIP-1271 so Passport and Sigil (C7) Safes can delegate credit.
4. Draws. A spender calls draw(amount, to).
- The account checks expiry, period usage, the spender's outstanding amount and the recipient lock.
- It checks that post-draw LTV ≤ min(maxLtv, 70% of LLTV) using the market oracle.
- It then calls Morpho.borrow(market, amount, 0, onBehalf = account, receiver = to).
- Spenders have no code path to withdraw collateral or to send funds elsewhere.
5. Repay and revoke.
- Anyone can repay(amount) with a MUSD permit, which calls Morpho.repay with onBehalf = account.
- Optional auto-repay draws from the owner's wsMUSD when LTV crosses a threshold.
- revokeCredit(spender) cuts access instantly. Only the owner can withdraw collateral.
6. Integrations.
- x402: an SDK and MCP tool let an agent draw just in time to its own EOA within its allowance, then pay through facilitator.vativ.io (MUSD domain 'Mezo USD' v1, settlement proxy 0x4020…0001, gas sponsored).
- Checkout and subscription contracts call draw directly, so 'pay with BTC credit' needs no MUSD balance. This makes Tab a funding source for the 13+ payment entries.
- Mezo ID names spenders and recipients (resolved server-side).
- A card-processor role with daily limits serves Mezo's card roadmap.
7. Keepers handle liquidations via Morpho.liquidate (or C1's backstop) and auto-repay.

- ICreditAllowance and TabAccount: any app, agent or card integrates with a single draw() call.
- Per-spender Draw and Repay events: a public history of credit usage [I], raw material for Luongo's creditworthiness line of thought.
- The Morpho market ID, shared with C1 if C1 is built.
